adjudication_label: batch_2:Lattice distortion and atomic displacement in refractory HEAs
canonical_question: Is the mean atomic displacement of 0.018 nm cited from Ref. [35] for HfNbTaTiZr derived at 300 K or a different temperature?

question_variants.question: Is the mean atomic displacement of 0.018 nm cited from Ref. [35] for HfNbTaTiZr derived at 300 K or a different temperature?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text cites the value of 0.018 nm and attributes it to Ref. [35], describing it as derived from ab-initio lattice distortion, but it does not specify the temperature (e.g., 300 K) at which this calculation was performed in the cited reference. The text only mentions 'expected thermal values' as a comparison point without stating the reference temperature for the 0.018 nm value.

answers.answer: The text states that for HfNbTaTiZr, an ab-initio lattice distortion leading to atomic displacements with a mean value of 0.018 nm was reported in Ref. [35], but it does not specify the temperature at which this value was derived. It only notes the value is much larger than expected thermal values.
answers.boundary_limitation: Temperature of the cited ab-initio calculation is not specified in the text.
evidence_spans: In the present study, we focus on the effect of chemical SRO on the vibrational density of states and the phonon heat conductivity in a prototypical refractory HEA, HfNbTaTiZr, which crystallizes in the bcc structure [3] , [43] , [44] . Using an atomistic model of this alloy, we are able to study, besides the random alloy, various degrees of chemical SRO in the alloy. As a result, we show that chemical SRO can modify the heat conductivity in a sizable way.
